name: Fundamentals of Data Structures
topics: Data Structure Basics and Algorithm Complexity
Define data structure; differentiate linear and non-linear data structures and discuss two in detail.
Explain the complexity of algorithms and the time–space trade-off; give the time complexity of the given code segment.
Arrays: Memory Representation and Operations
How is an array represented in memory? Differentiate row-major and column-major order and find the address of the given element.
Write an algorithm for insertion at the end and deletion at the front of an array; list merits and demerits of array implementation of lists.
Linked Lists
Write an algorithm to insert a node at the end of a singly linked list; compare singly and circular linked lists.
Write a program to reverse a circular linked list / return the nth element of a doubly linked list; list advantages and applications of linked lists.
Stacks and Expression Conversion
Implement PUSH and POP on a stack using an array and analyse the complexity; list stack applications.
Convert the given infix expression to prefix and postfix, and evaluate the given postfix expression using a stack.
Queues and Priority Queues
Differentiate a queue and a priority queue; implement a priority queue using linked lists.
Implement a linear queue using arrays; what is the problem with it and how is it solved?
Trees: BST, Traversals, AVL and Threaded Trees
Insert the given keys into an empty BST and show the result of deleting the root; write the BST search/insert algorithm.
Construct the expression tree for the given expression and give its preorder, inorder and postorder traversals; explain AVL and threaded binary trees.
Searching and Sorting
Write insertion sort / selection sort with an example and analyse its complexity.
Explain binary search and the best and worst cases of merge sort with examples.
Hashing and Collision Resolution
Define hashing and explain why it is needed.
Discuss collision resolution techniques with examples.
Graphs: Representation, Shortest Paths and Spanning Trees
Give two representations of graphs and define in-degree and out-degree; illustrate Dijkstra's algorithm with an example.
What is a minimum spanning tree? Explain Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms with examples; illustrate topological sort.
